experiment: A/B retrieval on valid split, plain-BERT checkpoint (results/bert_model, retrained 2026-07-09), speaker-rate overrides on, chromadb off
conclusion: Inference-time evidence concatenation HURTS a statement-only-trained BERT, monotonically with evidence length: encyclopedic text biases predictions toward REAL (recall collapses). Better retrieval coverage makes this WORSE, not better. Evidence must be present at TRAINING time (bert_film_rag.py, text-pair encoding) for the model to learn to use it. This also reinterprets the historical RAG +1.4pp over plain BERT: with ~50% retrieval misses the model often saw no evidence, and gains likely came from the metadata/fact-check overrides.
